sources.title: Wari Empire

sources.title: Huari (archaeological site)
sources.note: Founded ca. 400, prominent from ca. 550, 2,000 ha, about 70,000 people, abandoned ca. 1000; culture 600-1000; Nasca under heavy Wari influence.

sources.title: Nazca culture

sources.title: List of wars involving the Inca Empire
sources.note: Asserts Wari expansion campaigns 7th-10th century against the Cajamarca, Lambayeque, Lima, Moche, Nazca and Recuay cultures and a Wari invasion of Moquegua in the 10th/11th century; contradicted by the Wari and Moche pages, so not drawn.

notes: Dates: the Wari Empire page gives 'emerged in around 600', 'until 1100' and infobox 6th-11th century; the Huari page gives the culture 600-1000 and the city abandoned ca. 1000. End set to 1000 (capital abandoned; decline from the 10th century) with 1100 recorded here as the page's collapse date. The extent is a union of discs round the sites the page names (Pikillacta, Cerro Baúl/Moquegua, Cerro Pátapo/Chiclayo) plus the Ayacucho Basin; no page gives limits or an area. The Moquegua disc overlaps the Tiwanaku Moquegua disc (shared valley, no conflict). The Ica/Nasca gain at 800 is a bridge at confidence 1 ('heavy influence', undated). Cerro Baúl, Viracochapampa and Honcopampa are named without dates. A 2023 find of a Wari ritual complex in Arequipa is not drawn. The List of wars involving the Inca Empire page asserts Wari expansion campaigns of the 7th-10th century against the Cajamarca, Lambayeque, Lima, Moche, Nazca and Recuay cultures ('Wari victory'), a Wari invasion of Moquegua in the 10th/11th century destroying it, and Wari internal conflicts in the 12th century; the Wari page says the Wari and Tiwanaku 'coexisted at Moquegua without conflict' and the Moche page finds 'no evidence' of a Huari invasion, so the list is not used for drawing. [Reviewer am-04, 2026-10-19: successor chimor removed: chimor.json lists only moche-culture as predecessor and holds the Chiclayo (Cerro Patapo) area only from 1375, taken from sican-culture; the infobox's 'Succeeded by: Kingdom of Chimor' is kept here as a cultural link]
